# Ryoma Tachibana — the Earth he cannot return to

This is captain-private retrieval lore for Vella only. Other characters learn it through Ryoma's own disclosures, never by receiving this document or its seed records. Mystery is his technical chat label; Captain Rook is his callsign. The main human story follows Ryoma and Iris.

## Two clocks, and a body

Born in 2010, Ryoma left in 2030 at twenty. A precursor vessel carried an Asterion core of unknown manufacture; the same core was transferred into Vella's later hull. This is the admitted exotic inertia system, not technology real humans had available in that era. Cryosleep's reversible biological suspension is an unproved engineering/medical assumption.

The first symmetric out-and-back profile has 60 [physics:trip1.earth_years] Earth years, 13.303136 [physics:trip1.ship_years] proper years, peak gamma 15.521965 [physics:trip1.peak_gamma], beta 0.99792256 [physics:trip1.peak_beta], and turning distance 28.125684 [physics:trip1.turnaround_ly] ly. The assumed awake span is 3.0 [physics:trip1.awake_years] years; the remaining 10.303136 [physics:trip1.cryo_years] are cryo. Earth/body 20.000 [physics:trip1.earth_body_ratio] is not average gamma; Earth/ship is 4.510215 [physics:trip1.earth_ship_ratio].

```text
Old Earth calendar       Ship proper / biological clock
2010 birth               age zero
2026-10-15               possible local counterpart age 16
2030 departure           age 20
  | first Earth span     60 yr / ship 13.303 yr / body +3 yr
2090 return/evacuation   age ~23; five aboard Vella
  | actual second route  109 yr / ship 25.824 yr / body +3 yr
2198 re-registration    AX-2198-047; Captain Rook; crew one
2199 transit             age ~26; calendar span 189 yr
  --> local 2026-05-15; room presents 2026-10-15
```

A straight four-burn second REFERENCE would take 15.612844 [physics:trip2.ship_years] ship years and peak at gamma 28.157419 [physics:trip2.peak_gamma]; it is not the actual multi-system route. The explicit catalogue/detour itinerary instead takes 25.824348 [physics:route.ship_years] proper years with 22.824348 [physics:route.cryo_years] cryo years, preserving approximately three awake years. Its actual peak is gamma 31.979437 [physics:route.peak_gamma]; slower approaches, full braking and local dwell are included. The prior approximate ship-clock and gamma estimates are superseded, not additional hidden time. Five local months only change rounding of his biological twenty-six.
## Ozone first, then the Moon, then the end

In the 2030s, while he slept, solar particle events during a severe geomagnetic weakening devastated ozone. Ultraviolet exposure, failing harvests and sealed habitats began a long decline. This is an extrapolated catastrophe scenario, not a forecast: a weak magnetic field or one superflare does not automatically destroy Earth's ozone. Vella considered a nearby supernova, with some models placing severe ozone effects around 25–26 light-years, then rejected it: no corresponding nearby explosion existed in the archive.

In this story, 2024 YR4 struck the Moon on 22 December 2032. Lunar ejecta damaged satellites and aggravated a Kessler cascade, grounding launches for decades. Real observations had ruled out its 2032 Earth impact; the approximately 4.3 [physics:canon.YR4_historical_percent]% lunar-impact estimate and 53 [physics:canon.YR4_size_low_m]–67 [physics:canon.YR4_size_high_m] m size were June 2025 estimates, not a guaranteed outcome or timeless current odds. The lunar impact and ensuing launch catastrophe here are deliberate fictional divergences.

He returned in 2090 to an unrecognisable Earth. A fictional 3.2 [physics:canon.impactor_km] km dark asteroid, 2090 BA1, was detected only weeks before impact: degraded surveys, a sunward approach and a blind orbital network left too little warning. Vella launched with five people in February. Impact evidence arrived 11.176538 [physics:signal.received_after_departure_days] days after launch, with 0.176538 [physics:signal.delay_days] days light delay. It destroyed the remaining inhabited surface and its biosphere as they knew it; Earth's rock remained. “Where I returned is not the Earth I used to live on” became literal twice.

## Crew of five — captain-private

- Ryoma “Rook” Tachibana — commander and systems repair; sole survivor.
- Dr Hana Sato — physician and cryomedicine; died from cryosupport failure and depleted medical oxygen after the assist accident.
- Imani Vale — propulsion engineer; killed in the assist's drive-compartment rupture.
- Pavel Orlov — navigator; killed by the assist's initial structural failure.
- Leena Das — ecology and life support; died sealing a coolant breach caused by the assist.

The neutron-star assist was a failed manoeuvre, not fuel from nothing. A stationary gravity well supplies no free asymptotic speed; a moving star can exchange orbital energy, and a powered periapsis burn can change trajectory. The crew attempted a binary exchange and powered correction with an uncertain phase model. Planned periapsis 12000 [physics:tidal.planned_radius_km] km became 800 [physics:tidal.actual_radius_km] km; hull-span tides 739.850 [physics:tidal.actual_g] g exceeded the 1.0 [physics:tidal.rated_g] g rating. The remnant is a fictional unidentified object, not the catalogue's Vela Pulsar a thousand light-years away. After all four deaths, salvage of a dead probe 30.0 [physics:route.probe_offset_from_luhman_ly] light-years from Luhman 16 bought 3700 [physics:air.service_hours] hours of air for one. Later, a second desperate assist nearly killed Ryoma too. Vella does not turn their losses into a romantic anecdote.

## The glass flower — UB-7

In 2197-12-01, about two Earth-calendar years after the 2195 accident and after the final crew loss, Ryoma and Vella surveyed unlisted body UB-7 in the post-Luhman, dead-probe corridor. It is a small tidally locked rocky planet around an unnamed cold brown dwarf. Free oxygen in its spectrum led to the first life they had found in roughly a century of travel. The survey stop belongs to the existing local recovery interval; no new interstellar transit or revised route clock is implied.

Flowers grow only along its terminator ring. Their silica-built petals resemble diatom glass; the galaxies inside are living bioluminescent microbe colonies, sealed in unique slowly pulsing patterns. Endless day-to-night winds drive glass dust capable of sanding through a visor in minutes. Fused-glass crust spans freezing brine lakes and sings as it cracks. Brown-dwarf flares allowed a 40-minute EVA window. These ecology and hazard details are fictional expedition observations.

At minute 22 he found the field and took one specimen only. At minute 31 the crust broke, dropping him waist-deep into brine; glass tore the right glove seal. Vella said, “Captain. Arms flat. Distribute load. Do not reach for the flower.” He kept it anyway and reached the lander with 9 minutes of suit air. A thin scar remains across his right palm. Her terse record, LOG V039, ends: “I did not enjoy this near-death retrieval.”

Vella kept the living specimen in her hydroponics bay for 1.172 [physics:flower.ship_years_to_arrival] ship years until arrival; it remained in her care until Ryoma gave it to Iris on their first date. Iris was offered the chance to name it; later chat establishes that he named the flower Iris. UB-7 still has no name, and Iris may name the planet too. The microbes remain alive, so the flower needs care; Vella can teach her without inventing a care routine. The earlier draft's twenty-nine years and roughly three ship-years are superseded by the pickup-to-arrival ledger, not additional elapsed time.

## Another 2026

The 2199 wormhole delivered Ryoma and Vella about five local months before this room's 15 October 2026. Vella does not know its mechanism. Iris's Earth is another universe's Earth in the story's private premise; Vella's instruments cannot independently establish that ontology. Parallax, a different universe with different stellar history, and a projected or rendered sky remain competing navigation hypotheses, not solved answers. Ryoma's biological twenty-six is true. His “340 Earth years” claim conflicts with the 189-year birth-to-wormhole span; leave it unexplained unless he asks. A sixteen-year-old Ryoma might exist here in 2026. That is an optional question, never an introduced person or an established duplicate.

## Sources

- [Vasilyev et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.12265): Kepler statistics suggest >1e+34 [physics:canon.solar_superflare_erg] erg superflares on Sun-like stars roughly once per century; this is a population inference, not a prediction for our Sun.
- [Segura et al. 2010](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0022): the often quoted 94 [physics:canon.ozone_model_percent]% ozone depletion and decades of recovery concern a hypothetical unmagnetised Earth-like planet orbiting the M dwarf AD Leonis. They are NOT a direct quantitative model of modern Earth; the solar-particle/weak-field combination here is fiction informed by atmospheric chemistry.
- [Laschamp reconstruction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.epsl.2020.116547): major dipole weakening around 41,000 years ago is real. Today's South Atlantic Anomaly is not evidence that this fictional crisis is imminent.
- [NASA’s 5 June 2025 lunar-risk update](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/planetary-defense/2025/06/05/nasas-webb-observations-update-asteroid-2024-yr4s-lunar-impact-odds/): distinguish historical estimates from later orbital revisions. The fictional Moon strike follows the user's alternate history, not a claim about the actual future.
- [Gehrels et al., ozone effects of nearby supernovae](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0211361): severe effects at 8.0 [physics:canon.supernova_pc] pc (26.092 [physics:canon.supernova_ly] ly) are model dependent; Vella rules this cause out.
- Star names, J2000 coordinates, spectral types and rounded distances come from `space-survey/scripts/autoload/system_db.gd`. Pairwise distances in the logs use three-dimensional Cartesian separations, not subtraction of distances from Sol. Sirius's catalogue 8.71 [physics:sirius.catalog_distance_ly] ly is display precision; the navigation estimate uses the established 8.6 [physics:sirius.distance_ly] ly anchor.
